reason: The local material needs to be gathered for paving, so using the shovel on the workshop ground seems like a practical first step.
expectation: I expect to collect or expose local material, though I am not sure what form it will take.

alternatives.reason: The mesh and metal stock might make a screen for preparing the material, but I want to gather it first.

effect: The shovel produced excavated regolith, giving me material to prepare for paving.
reaction: That result was straightforward; I’m curious how the material will be processed.
reason: Combining the mesh with metal stock is the only available combination, and it seems likely to make a screen for the regolith.
expectation: I expect to make a screening tool, though I’m unsure how it will be used.

effect: The mesh and stock made a regolith sieve, confirming how the material can be prepared.
reaction: The result was predictable, but it makes the next step clear.
reason: Sieving the excavated regolith is the only offered combination and should separate it by particle size.
expectation: I expect screened regolith suitable for further processing, though I don't know what fractions the game will produce.

effect: The sieve produced a consistent fine feedstock, making a furnace trial possible.
reaction: The explanation of why particle consistency matters made the sieving step more satisfying.
reason: The furnace trial is the only offered combination and should test the prepared regolith for paving.
expectation: I expect the furnace to heat the graded regolith into a paving material, though I don't know whether it will need further processing.

effect: The furnace produced usable bricks after a slower firing cycle, and the next goal is to make a solid workshop floor.
reaction: The failed first trial made the process more interesting, and the distinction between a floor and an airtight structure was useful.
reason: Putting the bricks on the workshop ground directly addresses the new floor goal.
expectation: I expect to lay the bricks into a solid workshop floor, though the result may require another step.

alternatives.reason: The metal stock might help build supports or another structure, but the ground placement seems more directly relevant to the floor.

effect: The bricks became workshop paving, completing the floor goal and the chapter.
reaction: Finishing the floor was satisfying, though the result added little detail.

mostWorthwhile.text: The furnace trial was most worthwhile: the failed first firing and slower successful cycle showed that the process needed adjustment, while the porous bricks were suitable for a floor but not for holding an atmosphere.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making and using the sieve felt predictable because each was the only offered combination, although the explanation of consistent feedstock gave the work a purpose.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the first firing flaked and a slower cycle produced sound bricks.

arbitrary.text: No action felt clearly arbitrary; even the sequential preparation steps had a plausible purpose.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the practical details of processing local material made me curious how the workshop and root beds might develop.
